title: Recipe and Group Chat
premise: Wren Delacroix, a nonbinary baker's kid who channels feelings into bread, has spent fifteen years being so careful it hurts — until a school group chat begins predicting events that haven't happened yet. The messages turn out to be echoes from a fire that killed three students decades ago, buried by the school board to protect its own reputation. As the predictions grow darker and start targeting Wren's friends, they must decode the chat's warnings, expose what the board covered up, and accept that survival has always cost them something: their voice, their history, and finally their invisibility. In the end, Wren bakes a memorial loaf with the victims' names braided into the crust, forcing the town to remember — even though remembering means Wren can never be careful again.
about_author: Dominic Thornbury is a former night-shift baker who writes young adult fiction about queer kids outlasting the institutions meant to protect them. They live in a small river town where every bakery still keeps one recipe no one will explain.

chapters.title: The Loaf That Knew
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren bakes grief-bread for a classmate's canceled memorial and notices the dough rising toward the oven door like it's reaching for something. That night, an unknown number adds them to a group chat called 'Class of '89.' Emotional beat: quiet unease beneath Wren's practiced calm; the first crack in their careful life.

chapters.title: Messages From Tuesday
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The chat predicts a water main break in the gym parking lot — hours before it happens. Wren's best friend Priya dismisses it as a prank until the timestamp checks out. Emotional beat: vertigo and denial; Wren realizes being careful never protected anyone from things that arrive early.

chapters.title: What the Board Buried
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya digs into microfilm and finds a 1989 chemistry lab fire that killed three students, scrubbed from the school's official history. The board's minutes end mid-sentence that week. Emotional beat: righteous anger; the discovery that erasure is a decision someone made on purpose.

chapters.title: Careful Is a Kind of Hunger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A flashback chapter braided into present-day baking: how Wren learned, after their aunt's disappearance, that wanting things loudly gets people taken away. The chat sends its first personal message: 'You bake like her.' Emotional beat: fear turning inward; identity as something Wren has been rationing.

chapters.title: The Third Prediction
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV rotating through Wren, Priya, and Marcus, a skeptic on the newspaper staff. The chat predicts a locker will 'open wrong' — and Marcus finds the 1989 victims' untouched lockers welded shut behind the gym wall. Emotional beat: dread made physical; the past has an address.

chapters.title: Smoke Signals
chapters.summary: Marcus's POV. Inside the wall cavity: scorched notebooks, a student's diary naming a teacher who locked the lab door during the fire — a teacher who later joined the school board. The chat goes silent. Emotional beat: the thrill of proof curdling into danger as someone reports them to administration.

chapters.title: Detention for the Dead
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. The principal threatens expulsion and confiscates the diary; Wren's parents, terrified of attention, side with the school. Alone, Wren bakes bread with rage instead of care for the first time — and it's the best thing they've ever made. Emotional beat: the price of survival revealed as complicity; Wren chooses not to pay it anymore.

chapters.title: Countdown in Crumbs
chapters.summary: Wren and Priya's alternating POV. The chat returns with a final prediction: 'Friday. Room 114. It happens again unless someone reads the names aloud.' They realize the loop repeats because the fire was never acknowledged. Emotional beat: desperate momentum; time running out in flour-dusted hours.

chapters.title: Room 114
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, climax. At the board meeting, Wren interrupts with the memorial loaf and reads the victims' names as the sprinklers fail overhead — the old wiring sparking exactly as predicted. Wren drags the board president back from the locked lab door, breaking the pattern by refusing to let history repeat unwatched. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into witness; survival redefined as speaking.

chapters.title: Bread for the Living
chapters.summary: Wren's POV, resolution. The board resigns; a real memorial is built, and the chat sends one last message — 'Thank you. You can close the thread now' — before dissolving. Wren teaches Priya to braid dough, no longer careful, just open. Emotional beat: grief integrated, identity claimed; memory as the recipe that keeps everyone alive.
